reason: Each of the five mental-factor groups is explained at length with definitions, functions, subdivisions, cited verses and answered objections.
The three children are one-line glosses (by function, time, teaching) of why citta, manas and vijnana are named differently; the remaining text concerns the parent topic.
The scripture and reasoning children each set out the Vaibhasika proof that attainment is substantial and the Master's rebuttal, a real argument.
The first child is a one-line definition but the second argues at length about non-obstruction as cause, with objections, replies and an analogy.
Most of the eight occasions are one-line definitions, but the emerging-from-absorption and rebirth-linking children analyse which minds follow which across realms at length.
The children explain the twenty minds, debate whether the twelve or twenty is wider, and analyse at length how the twelve minds are obtained.
Each realm (desire, form, formless) is described at length with its abodes, cited verses, divergent views and objections answered.
The children discuss the five destinies and the stations of consciousness and abodes of beings at length, raising and answering many doubts.
After a short identification, the proof child argues at length for the existence of the intermediate state with scripture, reasoning and rebuttals.
The children explain at length the features of the intermediate being and the manner of entering the womb, with citations and objections.
Each of the six children is an extended explanation of dependent origination (types, threefold grouping, cause and effect, sutra meaning, links, examples).
The children discuss the mind at death, the manner of dying and what follows death, with arguments and cited verses.
The children describe the mountains, oceans and continents of the receptacle world at length with measurements, cited verses and divergent views.
